thread:
maria: starting migration: events.payload -> change type TEXT->JSONB (safe parse). change window 01:30-02:45 UTC. tagging @alex @devon for DB ops; @sam for rollout cadence.

alex: noted. will run canary on replica-set-b at 01:35, validate parse failure rates and lock hold times.

deploybot: job scheduled: mig_2026_12_events_payload_jsonb on runner-7. auto-stop triggers: exclusive_lock>20s or parse_error_rate>0.5%.

devon: backfill approach: streaming small batches with try_parse -> on failure write to quarantine table `events.payload_bad` and continue. target rate 3k rows/min.

sam: timeline: canary (1 shard) -> pause 4m -> wave 1 (10 shards) -> pause 6m -> remaining. communicate to clients to allow schema-flexible reads for 2h.

tess: adding release notes blurb: "events.payload migrated to jsonb (parse failures quarantined); opt-in strict parsing flag for clients."

alex: preflight on staging showed ALTER lock median 90ms; but one shard had 12s during vacuum. we'll watch autovacuum and long-running ANALYZE.

deploybot: canary started 01:35:10. running: ALTER TABLE events ALTER COLUMN payload TYPE jsonb USING payload::jsonb;

srebot: alert: migration job mig_2026_12_events_payload_jsonb observed exclusive_lock_duration=22s on shard-3 at 01:36:41. auto-stop engaged.

devon: looks like a concurrent UNLOGGED insert from pipeline-collector overlapped. I see lots of `COPY` in pg_stat_activity.

alex: can we pause the collector? it's in non-critical window but mis-scheduled. tagging @infra for immediate hold.

maria: pause collector, but don't kill without notice. checklist to unblock: 1) pause conflicting writer 2) ensure replica lag <4s 3) run single-column ALTER retry on canary 4) run quick validate query for parse errors: `SELECT count(*) FROM events WHERE payload::jsonb IS NULL` (should be 0) 5) observe write p99 for 4m. agree?

sam: +1. also note: if parse_error_rate >0 then we keep quarantine policy and continue; rollback only if lock or latency thresholds breached.

tess: documenting rollback steps: 1) stop backfill 2) restore original column type via `ALTER TABLE events ALTER COLUMN payload TYPE text USING payload::text;` 3) remove feature flag; 4) postmortem. adding to runbook.

deploybot: operator hold requested by alex, reason="paused collector". manual unblock allowed once infra confirms pause.

infra-bot: collector pipeline flagged and paused (job-id 8932).

alex: running ALTER retry on shard-3 at 01:40:02.

deploybot: ALTER retry completed at 01:40:12. duration 210ms. p99 write latency spike 1.1s (exceeded 1s threshold) -> marking degraded.

maria: since p99>1s, we should not continue auto-rollout. decision point: rollback vs. manual throttle. options: A) rollback immediately and pin API to old behavior B) keep column as jsonb on canary, reduce backfill rate to 1k/min and re-evaluate in 15m. Thoughts?

devon: recommend B — we can enable quarantine and slower rate to avoid blocking writers. rollback will be painful for clients that already read jsonb.

sam: ops preference B with a hard stop: if p99 >1.2s again or any exclusive_lock>18s we rollback. also schedule a postmortem.

tess: note for release notes: include rollback trigger and owners (alex rollback lead, devon data recovery).

alex: agree with B. I'll reduce backfill to 1k/min and resume only on remaining shards after a successful 15m watch.

deploybot: backfill rate adjusted to 1000 rows/min per worker. resuming staggered apply: next wave scheduled in 16m.

srebot: watching metrics. automated rollback policy still available. will page if thresholds exceeded.

15m later...
srebot: metrics update: p99 write latency stabilized at 0.78s; no exclusive locks >12s seen.

deploybot: resumed wave-1 (10 shards).
devon: backfill progress: 22% complete. quarantine table rows: 12 (will triage).

maria: good progress. decision: do not pin API version now; clients get tolerant reads. we'll only pin if we trigger rollback. keep release notes draft open.

1h later...
deploybot: migration job completed: 100% shards converted; 99.5% rows backfilled; quarantine table 18 rows for manual remediation. created follow-up ticket DATA-879 to handle quarantined rows.
tess: finalizing release notes: mention quarantine flow, follow-up ticket, and runtime thresholds. publishing at 04:00 UTC. :tada:
maria: closing thread. owners and rollback steps in thread. thanks for fast coordination.
